(Xinhua/Mao Siqian) GUANGZHOU, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- Chinese tech giant Huawei on Monday launched the Mate XT 2 tri-fold smartphone powered by the new Kirin 9050 Pro chip, the first high-performance processor to use logic folding technology. The Kirin 9050 Pro stacks logic units in layers within a single chip, shortening signal transmission paths, reducing latency and boosting overall performance, according to a launch event in Guangzhou. The last time Huawei introduced a new Kirin chip at a flagship launch was at the global release of the Mate 40 smartphone six years ago. The company has continued to innovate and break new ground in recent years. The company's research and development (R&D) spending accelerated sharply to reach 121.38 billion yuan (17.9 billion U.S. dollars) in the first half of 2026, marking a record high for the period and accounting for more than a quarter of revenue. Huawei is advancing rapidly across multiple technology-intensive fields, including artificial intelligence, chips, operating systems and smart vehicles, with its sustained R&D intensity laying the groundwork for long-term technological capability. The strategy appears to be paying off in the market. According to IDC data, Huawei's smartphone shipments grew 19.4 percent year on year in the second quarter of 2026, pushing its market share to 22.6 percent -- the top position in China. item.title: China improves investment mechanism to advance rural revitalization
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- China has unveiled a plan to improve its investment mechanism for rural revitalization as part of broader efforts to boost agricultural and rural development, the country's agriculture ministry said Monday. Jointly issued by multiple government bodies, including the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, the National Development and Reform Commission and the People's Bank of China, the plan calls for stronger fiscal and financial support and increased social capital participation. The goal is to steadily boost investment in rural revitalization and further optimize the investment structure for agriculture, rural areas and farmers. By 2030, the country aims to have basically established a rural revitalization investment mechanism aligned with agricultural and rural development conditions, featuring a well-balanced structure, sound approaches and an emphasis on both efficiency and effectiveness, according to the plan. Emphasizing the leading role of government funding, the plan outlines measures to fully leverage bonds, loans and insurance to support agricultural and rural development, while calling for coordinated efforts by governments, financial institutions and social capital. Favorable pricing and subsidy policies will also be rolled out in a more coordinated and effective manner, according to the plan. Addressing issues concerning agriculture, rural areas and farmers remains a top priority on China's development agenda, with advancing rural revitalization across the board serving as a key task. To this end, the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) stresses improving the effectiveness of policies aimed at strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching rural areas. It calls for improving related mechanisms and policy frameworks, facilitating the two-way flow of resources between urban and rural areas, and injecting greater vitality into agricultural and rural development. ■

item.title: China's Xinjiang accelerates clean energy push amid national green transition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
URUMQI, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- A short drive west of Korla in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, a vast desert landscape has been transformed into a shimmering sea of solar panels, underscoring the region's green energy push. Operated by PetroChina Tarim Oilfield, the 1.3-gigawatt photovoltaic (PV) project in the Shangku high-tech zone is one of the largest in Xinjiang and the oilfield's first million-kilowatt-class plant. Spanning 35,000 mu (about 2,333 hectares), the facility has generated over 1.6 billion kWh of clean power since connecting to the grid in January 2025. Inside its centralized control room, real-time data enables full-process digital management, with just a few staff members overseeing the extensive site using intelligent cleaning robots and drones for routine inspection. Lei Ting, executive director of Tarim Oilfield's new energy department, said the company is expanding green power supply systems to help build a zero-carbon industrial park, offering a replicable model for low-carbon transformation in the petrochemical sector. The Shangku project is one of many across Xinjiang. From the 1-gigawatt wind-solar hub near the region's capital Urumqi to the 4-gigawatt solar farm in southern Xinjiang's Ruoqiang County, these initiatives exemplify the region's commitment to a low-carbon future. By the end of 2025, Xinjiang had built six 10-gigawatt-class renewable energy bases spanning the entire region, with total installed renewable capacity reaching 169 million kilowatts, or 64 percent of its total power capacity. As a key generating end of China's west-to-east power transmission endeavor, Xinjiang had cumulatively transmitted 304.36 billion kWh of renewable electricity to other regions as of March 18, 2026, accounting for roughly 30 percent of its total outbound power supply, according to the local branch of State Grid. In 2025, Xinjiang's green power trading volume reached 43.43 billion kWh, a surge of 230 percent year on year, and a record high equivalent to saving 13.13 million tonnes of standard coal consumption and cutting 35.47 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions, Xinjiang Power Exchange Center noted. Nationwide, by the end of 2025, China's total installed wind and solar capacity had reached 1.84 billion kilowatts, surpassing thermal power for the first time in history. "Renewable energy has laid a 'green foundation' for Xinjiang's economic development, unlocking tremendous momentum for green transition and high-quality growth, while better benefiting people's livelihoods and fostering social cohesion," said Song Xueqiang, director of the Xinjiang Power Exchange Center's trading department. Xinjiang's efforts are part of China's broader strategy to build large-scale wind and solar power bases in its desert regions, a very important pillar of the national green transition. "We are planning a large-scale renewable energy export base in southern Xinjiang, integrating wind, solar, gas-fired and pumped-storage hydropower to build a gas-supported clean energy hub that serves national energy security and the green transition," Lei said. ■

item.title: International journalists witness China's rescue efforts in mudslide-ravaged Gyirong
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
GYIRONG, Xizang, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- Even with prior knowledge of the catastrophe, Brazilian journalist Bruno Falci Bitarelli Medeiros was struck by the harsh rescue conditions after a bumpy 12-hour bus ride from Lhasa to the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. The final stretch wound through rugged mountain roads, unpredictable weather and falling rocks. "It's a very difficult condition for the workers, and I very much admired how they keep searching for people," Medeiros said. Medeiros was among a group of journalists from international media outlets including CNN, Reuters and NBC who visited the devastated port from Saturday to Sunday. At a media briefing by the local emergency rescue headquarters, they heard from technical experts and local officials about ongoing efforts on multiple fronts: the search for the missing, victim identification, community assistance and secondary disaster prevention. The fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port in Xigaze City on the China-Nepal border on Aug. 26. As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, 43 people were confirmed dead and 519 remained missing. SEARCH GOING ON At the core disaster zone, a 35-meter-high flood mark, roughly the height of a 12-story building, was scored into the cliff above the ruins. "Everything below the flood mark was originally underwater," said Norbu Tsering, deputy head of the emergency rescue headquarters and acting mayor of Xigaze City. "Power was gone. What you see now is what we've restored in the past couple of days." Land access to the port was restored on the morning of Sept. 2, allowing heavy machinery to move in and clear working areas. Mud deposits average four meters deep in the hardest-hit zone, with some areas reaching 16 meters. Inside the core area, vehicles and machinery are conducting deep-search operations -- excavating, searching and clearing layer by layer during grid-by-grid sweeps. Konda Jagan Mohan Varma from the Press Trust of India watched the operation. "The glacier breakdown brought down a lot of slush, mud and huge rocks together," he said. "A large part of infrastructure was damaged on both sides, in China and Nepal." He noted the scale of the rescue effort unfolding around him -- heavy machinery carving through the debris, teams fanning out across the ruins in methodical searches. Just an hour after the journalists arrived, the valley turned from sunshine to pounding rain, forcing an emergency evacuation. Rescuers have persisted in such conditions for more than 10 days. As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, China had deployed over 2,500 rescue personnel, more than 500 vehicle trips and over 9,000 sets of search equipment, and air-dropped more than 5 tonnes of supplies. Two people from a nearby village have been rescued, and nearly 1,000 personal items have been recovered. BEYOND BORDERS After repeated verification, authorities confirmed that 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries, including Nepal, India, Latvia, the United States and Britain, remain missing. For identification, each body is numbered, photographed and sampled for DNA and dental records at the scene. The headquarters has set up a dedicated identification team. So far, none of the bodies retrieved are foreign nationals. Responding to a question about the identification process for the missing, Yang Lahong, deputy director of the foreign affairs office of Xizang, said at the briefing that the names and specific information of missing foreigners have not been made public to protect their privacy, but have been shared with the relevant embassies through diplomatic channels. A 24-hour hotline for families of missing foreign nationals has received 509 calls, with feedback provided promptly, Yang added. At Nepal's request, the Chinese government has dispatched tunnel rescue and DNA testing experts to Nepal, along with emergency material assistance. Through a China-Nepal disaster prevention information notification mechanism, daily updates on meteorology, hydrology, glacial lakes and glaciers are shared with Nepal. After the disaster, many Nepalese border residents were stranded in China due to the port closure. Local authorities have seen to the daily needs of 1,720 Nepalese border residents. Green channels for foreign personnel entry and exit have been opened. A total of 3,388 foreign nationals originally planning to leave via Gyirong Port have been diverted, and authorities have helped 365 Nepalese border residents cross the border to return home. WATCHING FOR NEXT DANGER Preventing secondary disasters remains a priority. More than 170 experts and technicians are now monitoring the area with over 150 sets of equipment, including slope radar and drones. Along the main rescue route, 58 geological hazard spots have been identified, seven of them high-risk. Hu Bo, leader of the China Anneng rescue detection team, serves as a "sentinel" for frontline workers. When upstream data showed abnormal movement, he sounded the retreat signal. Whistles echoed through the gorge as personnel and machinery pulled back to safety zones. Hu said such scenarios can happen several times a night. Muhammad Asghar from the Associated Press of Pakistan observed the monitoring efforts. "The monitoring for secondary disasters is being done tirelessly, day and night," he said. On the site, Medeiros spotted civilian drones flying to observe potential risks for a secondary disaster. "The technology today is being very helpful to rescue operations in this disaster," he said. "Some countries use drones for war, but China uses drones to help people." Medeiros noted that, as global warming is the root cause of the disaster, more concrete actions from the world are needed to prevent these kinds of disasters from happening again, citing China's push for a green economy as an example. Asghar agreed. "Climate change is not the issue of only one country. The whole world should put their heads together," he said. ■

item.title: China's top court sets rules for AI deepfakes and other disputes
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- A familiar face on a video call may not be what it seems, as artificial intelligence (AI) can now replicate people's faces and voices with startling realism, creating new challenges for the law. On Monday, China's top court issued guidelines spelling out when such AI-generated content can lead to legal liability. The guidelines, released by the Supreme People's Court (SPC), address a range of emerging disputes, including AI deepfakes and voice cloning, algorithmic price discrimination and AI-generated false information. They make clear that people cannot use AI to create or distribute recognizable digital replicas of others without their consent, including cloned faces and voices. Such use constitutes an infringement of individuals' rights, while using AI-generated faces or voices to spread false claims or damage someone's reputation can also result in legal liability. China has already addressed such issues in court. In April 2024, the Beijing Internet Court ruled in the country's first AI-generated voice infringement case that using AI to recreate a person's identifiable voice without their consent can infringe upon their rights. China is a global leader in AI development. The size of the country's AI industry was estimated to exceed 1.2 trillion yuan (about 177 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, up 40 percent year on year. Also, China was home to more than 6,600 AI companies as of June 2026, representing 15 percent of the global total. The country has developed a complete industrial system spanning foundational infrastructure, models and frameworks, and sector-specific applications. The new rules come as AI-generated impersonation becomes increasingly easy to create and difficult to distinguish from authentic content. A handful of photographs or a short voice recording can provide enough material to produce a convincing digital replica. The guidelines also address algorithmic discrimination against consumers. Businesses that use algorithms to offer different prices or other transaction terms for the same goods or services without reasonable justification may be held liable if the practice causes harm to consumers. "We cannot expect every consumer to become an expert at spotting deception. The law must step in promptly to protect consumers' legitimate rights and interests," said Zhou Jiahai, head of the research office of the SPC. Another challenge is that generative AI systems can produce false or inaccurate information, commonly known as "AI hallucinations." AI service providers can be held liable if they are notified that their systems have generated content that infringes a person's rights but fail to take timely action. Users, too, can be held responsible for how they use AI. Anyone who deliberately uses prompts or other methods to induce an AI system to generate infringing content that harms others can be held liable. The guidelines also provide a way for people to seek swift protection when AI-generated content threatens to cause serious and irreversible harm. For example, someone whose face has been digitally altered and used to spread false and defamatory sexual claims may ask a court for an injunction if waiting to act could cause harm that would be difficult to repair later. China is advancing its "AI Plus" initiative to promote the extensive and in-depth integration of AI into various sectors and fields of the economy and society. As AI advances, governments worldwide are grappling with the challenge of encouraging innovation while also protecting people from potential harm. China has taken a series of steps to address the challenges posed by AI. In September 2025, it put into effect measures governing the labeling of AI-generated and synthesized content. The SPC's latest guidelines set out how courts should handle AI-related disputes, adding to China's evolving legal framework for AI. During the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in July, China stressed the need for adhering to the principles of openness and win-win and boosting innovation-driven development, strengthening risk awareness and ensuring that AI is secure and controllable, encouraging inclusiveness and promoting mutual learning between civilizations, and advocating solidarity and improving global governance. At the event, an action plan on international AI ethics governance was released. It calls on countries to take action in light of their national conditions in areas including ethical governance throughout the AI lifecycle, categorized and tiered risk prevention and control, the development of agile governance mechanisms, the cultivation of a collaborative ecosystem across industrial chains, and the fostering of a favorable social environment. As part of the efforts of China to implement the plan, stakeholders across industrial chains will be encouraged to clarify the boundaries of their rights and responsibilities. ■

item.title: China releases 5-year development plan for information, communications sector
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has issued a development plan for the information and communications industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) to promote the high-quality development of this sector. By 2030, a new-generation communications network with comprehensive coverage and leading performance is expected to be fully established, according to the plan, which has called for efforts to accelerate the development of a technologically advanced, secure and controllable information and communications industrial system. Meanwhile, an agile and efficient governance system integrating technology and management is expected to be effectively established, and network and data security capabilities featuring all-domain coordination and practical application will be significantly enhanced, the plan said. The industry's empowerment level and degree of globalization will be further improved, laying a solid foundation for basically achieving modernization of the information and communications sector by 2035, the plan added. The plan also outlines 13 key indicators, including achieving information and communications industry revenue of 4.1 trillion yuan (about 604.8 billion U.S. dollars) by 2030, cumulative investment of 3.8 trillion yuan in information infrastructure, and an average annual growth rate of 7 percent in total telecommunications business volume. By 2030, there will be 50 5G (including 5G-A) base stations per 10,000 people, intelligent computing power will reach 9,800 EFLOPS, and the 5G user penetration rate will reach 95 percent, the ministry said. EFLOPS, or ExaFLOPS, is a unit of computing performance, with each unit representing 1 quintillion floating-point operations per second. The plan lays out 26 key tasks across six major areas including information infrastructure construction as well as network and data security assurance. Among these, it specifically highlights the need to initiate 6G commercial services at an appropriate time and to accelerate the establishment of a nationwide integrated computing power network. Specific measures also include building an industry anti‑fraud laboratory and supporting enterprises to deeply promote the integration of artificial intelligence and manufacturing, the plan said. China has established the world's largest information infrastructure. Gigabit optical network access is available in every county, while 5G networks covers all towns and more than 95 percent of administrative villages. The country is pushing ahead with its Digital China initiative, aiming to raise the added value of the core industries of the digital economy to 12.5 percent of GDP by 2030, according to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). ■

item.title: Chinese premier meets Qatari PM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani in Beijing on Monday. Noting Qatar is an important strategic partner of China in the Middle East and the Gulf region, Li said China stands ready to work with Qatar to further enhance communication and coordination, firmly support each other on issues concerning each other's core interests, and advance bilateral relations to deliver greater benefits to the two peoples. Li called on the two sides to strengthen alignment of development strategies, advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and deepen collaboration in traditional energy, new-energy sources, infrastructure, artificial intelligence and finance to pursue win-win outcomes at a higher level. "China welcomes Qatari investment in China and supports more Chinese enterprises to invest in Qatar to improve the quality and efficiency of two-way investment," Li said, voicing hope that Qatar will continue to foster a sound development environment for Chinese enterprises and safeguard the safety of Chinese citizens, institutions and projects in Qatar. The two sides should also boost people-to-people and cultural exchanges covering culture, education, giant panda conservation and research to bring the peoples of the two countries closer, Li added. He said China supports Qatar's mediation efforts on Middle East issues and is ready to work with Qatar and other regional countries as well as the international community to strive for early peace and tranquility in the region. Al Thani said Qatar values its relations with China, and the two countries have consistently upheld mutual trust and respect and achieved mutual benefit and win-win results. He said Qatar is willing to work with China to scale up exchanges at all levels and deepen practical cooperation in economy and trade, high-and-new technologies and advanced manufacturing to jointly embrace the next golden decade of bilateral relations. Qatar commends and appreciates China's efforts to advance peace and stability in the Middle East, Al Thani said, adding that Qatar is committed to resolving conflicts through dialogue and restoring peace in the region. ■ Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen)

item.title: Book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization published
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- A book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization has been published by the Higher Education Press and the People's Publishing House. Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has approached ecological conservation from the perspective of ensuring the sustainable development of the Chinese nation. With a profound understanding of the important position and strategic significance of ecological conservation in the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics for a new era, the CPC Central Committee has vigorously advanced theoretical, practical and institutional innovation in this field, put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking and new strategies, led historic, transformative and comprehensive changes in China's ecological conservation, and developed Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization. The book introducing the thought, compiled under the organization of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee and the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, consists of an introduction and nine chapters, totaling about 170,000 Chinese characters. It systematically expounds on the significance, theoretical framework, essence, connotations and practical requirements of Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization. ■
